about.title: Windsor Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Sonoma County's most recent full-year data recorded one traffic death among the injury collisions logged in Windsor, a reminder that even a small town sees real loss on its streets. If that death happened because someone else was careless, whether on US-101, Old Redwood Highway, or a quieter neighborhood road, California law allows certain surviving family members to pursue a wrongful death claim. This is separate from any criminal case and focuses on the financial and emotional toll left behind. There's no cost to start a conversation, and no obligation. We know this is one of the hardest calls a family will make, and we try to make that first step as simple as possible.

whyChoose.title: What Windsor Families Should Understand About Wrongful Death Claims

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits who has standing to bring a wrongful death claim, generally a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in some cases. An attorney can help sort out who qualifies in your family's specific circumstances.

items.title: The Clock Starts at Two Years, Sometimes Less
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, but claims against a government entity, such as one involving a county road, carry a much shorter notice deadline. Acting sooner rather than later helps preserve those options.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Medical Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial costs, lost financial support the deceased would have provided, and compensation for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. An independent attorney can walk you through how these losses are typically calculated.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Windsor?
items.answer: Generally, California gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government entity, like Sonoma County or Caltrans, may be involved because of road conditions, the deadline to file a claim can be much shorter, sometimes just months. It's worth speaking to an attorney early to understand which timeline applies.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened on a smaller road like Shiloh Road instead of US-101?
items.answer: Not for purposes of whether you can file a claim, no. What matters is who was responsible and whether the death qualifies as wrongful under California law, regardless of whether it happened on a busy highway or a quieter local street. An attorney will look at the specific facts of the crash rather than the road name alone.

items.question: What can my family actually recover in a wrongful death case?
items.answer: California law allows recovery for funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have contributed, and non-economic losses like the loss of companionship, guidance, and care. Every family's losses look different, so an attorney will need to review your circumstances before discussing specifics. LawProactive can connect you with someone who handles these conversations directly.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case?
items.answer: No, they're separate processes. A criminal case, if one is filed, is brought by the state and focused on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by family members seeking compensation for their losses. One can proceed even if the other doesn't result in charges or a conviction.
